assay: LC-MS/MS protein identification, spectral counting from the deposit's PRIDE-filtered mzTab
licence: PRIDE/ProteomeXchange public-repository terms; no per-file notice located. Admitted with citation under the owner's decision of 2026-10-06 that every source is permitted with citation; the deposit and Guerreiro et al. 2014 are both cited.

citation.text: Guerreiro AC, Benevento M, Lehmann R, van Breukelen B, Post H, Giansanti P, Maarten Altelaar AF, Axmann IM, Heck AJ. Daily rhythms in the cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus probed by high-resolution mass spectrometry-based proteomics reveals a small defined set of cyclic proteins. Mol Cell Proteomics 2014;13(8):2042-2055. PRIDE PXD000510.

units: identified peptide-spectrum matches per million matches in the run (spectral counting), not TMT reporter-ion abundance

replicates.text: one TMT 6-plex per layer, its six channels being six sampling times inside that layer's window; the deposit's identification-only results do not separate the channels, so a layer has no replicate structure of its own

caveat: A spectral count, not an abundance, and not the study's own measurement. The deposit's generated mzTab files are mzTab-type Identification and carry no reporter-ion column, so the TMT 6-plex channels that resolved the time points are absent from the deposited results and exist only in the raw files. Each layer is therefore the pooled identification evidence of one 6-plex, covering the window its own metadata names, and the diel time resolution the study was designed around is lost. Shipped as pooled spectral counts by owner decision of 2026-10-07. Counting spectra measures abundance only coarsely and favours long and readily ionised proteins. Measured in PCC 7942, not UTEX 2973, and keyed by UniProt accession through UniProt's ordered-locus names and the one-to-one crosswalk.
